GOTO 2Packs Clear Assemble Display Boxes, Display Storage Cases, Stackable Show Cases for Pop Mart, Action Figures, Lego, Collectibles, Toys, Cosmetics (2 Boxes with 3 Partitions) We are avid collectors of Ninderoid and other anime figurines in this house. So when I thought I had found a hand on the wall view box for them I was excited. First, these are boxes that can not be hung on the wall. That was my bad for not reading carefully, but there isnt even a way to frankenstein them to hang on the wall and Why would you Not make even a hanger add on. There is a hole in the bottom for a light kit (which as of right now is not available) which would be cool, but again, if it is not able to hang on the wall not sure how it would easily sit on a table with a light attachment.
The two kits arrived well packaged but unfortunately both were cracked. The plastic is incredibly brittle and great care had to be used to fit these together. The door opens and closes nicely once assembled and it is very clear. The last thing that makes this less than a 5 star product is the shelving options. Two boxes, shipped with three half sized shelves. If you want to put something on it that needs a full shelf you must use two shelves. This leaves one half shelf for the second case. Again, i went online looking to purchase additional shelves so we could put figurines on them. I could not find them even on the manufacturer' page. What I noticed was a product designed to display specific (Very specific) products. And not terribly configurable. Overall, it is a decent display case for a shelf. But the fact the inner shelves are so thin (only measuring half the depth) and a two pack of cases comes only with three shelves is weird. Additionally the product is so brittle that I am not sure any form of shipping would prevent breakage the way it is shipped disassembled and flat.
If they come up with an additional iteration that can hang on a wall, or with the option to buy more shelves then yay great. (I was fully prepared to spend money to get this to work for me and my fam) Otherwise this kind of misses the mark for the cost.
Product free in exchange for an honest review

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Chutes and Ladders Board Game Like many of us over 40, we grew up with this game and recognize the graphics of the Classic Chutes and Ladders Board Game. Recently, after my dad passed, we cleared out our old house and found my old game. It followed my brother home to his family, but now I'm curious to compare the two.

Outside of nostalgia, the question is if the game stands on its own in 2015. My four year-old boy thinks so. He doesn't care about 1972 (or even know it existed, as time began with him, as he sees it). He begs to play it, right along with Trouble! and Legos.

Essentially, there's no strategy. The person going version has a small chance of winning, but for all intents and purposes, it is pure chance.

To move forward, the player spins from 1-6. Whatever square he might land on is either neutral, a ladder or a slide. Slides move him back to an earlier square, ladders move him up, and neutral squares allow him to stay put until the next move. There is no decision making.

Is it fun? Very much so, according to my boy. As there are 100 squares, there are plenty of opportunities to climb ladders and slide down. It is a little tricky to follow which direction to go, as the numbers start left-to-right, but zig-zag at each end. A patient older child or adult needs to be on-hand to help with game play.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Chutes and Ladders Board Game

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game The only bad thing about this game is the fact that my 2 year thinks it's a radio. We've had it for about a month now, and as I write this, it's "playing" in the background. It's playing in the background almost every night, if not during the day, too. It's super annoying! :P It's supposed to sound like ducks, I guess, but it's just lots of squeaking.

Otherwise, it's super cute, and my boys love playing it. I think 2-4 year old children will enjoy it the most, but it's labeled 3 and up. I imagine this is due to the stickers that must go on the ducks, and game board(which is a motorized pond). You do need batteries! There are 4 colors of stickers, 4 each. 3 of each will go on ducks and 1 on the game board. I wasn't paying attention enough to realize one of each color went on the game board. I ended up having to peel some stickers off of ducks.

You put the ducks on the game board, assign a color to each child(up to 4 players), and then press the center button. The ducks will then circle around the pond. Taking turns the child picks up a duck and turns it over. If it matches their assigned color, they keep it. If not, they put it back on the pond. While all the ducks are on the pond, it's a little crowded, so it was tough for my 2 year old to get the duck placed back on there without knocking over another duck, or several. It's easier to turn the pond off while your child is looking at the color and placing it back on the pond.

Overall, this is a fun game to teach a few colors, along with the art of taking turns and patience. My children had so much fun with it, they were impatient for their turn.
text_fidelity_b: Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game

Crayola Doodle Magic Lap Desk This is one horrible product! It's rare that I'm THIS disappointed in a toy for my children.

These markers are so light when used that your child can barely see what they've drawn! It's about as much fun as using a white crayon on a sheet of white paper, which is frustrating to a child! After a few minutes, both of my oldest boys(2 and 4) ended up just playing with the markers and stacking them on top of each other or putting them in their "holding" spot on the desk. Drawing, which is the purpose of this desk, wasn't the least bit of fun for them.

Since this was such a disappointment, I decided to take a chance on dry erase markers. Dry Erase markers **DO NOT** work with this desk! It doesn't come off. I'll keep trying to clean our board, and if I find something that works, I'll come back and let you know. Truly, THAT will be this toy's only saving grace. Otherwise, it's a total waste of money!

About the only thing I do like is the storage areas included. On the back of the desk, there is a holding spot for everything, except the washcloth. While in use, there's holding spots for the 4 markers that are included.

Another huge disappointment is that magic eraser. The magic solution looks a great deal like a bit of dishwashing liquid and water. When it runs out, though, it's gone. I twisted and turned and tried everything, short of breaking it, to get the magic eraser open for a refill. Apparently, it doesn't come open! I searched and couldn't find replacements, either. Such a disappointment!!

Overall, I can't recommend this product, unfortunately.

text_fidelity_a:
Marbleocity Triple Play Archimedes Screw Marble Machine Kit I like the idea of this toy/project more than I enjoyed the toy/project itself. It might provide an hour of entertainment to someone who liked to build models or tinker, and it is mildly educational, but it wasn't that much fun to put together, it was VERY SMALL, and it took a few tries to get it to work well. I would like to give it more stars because it's such a neat idea, but somehow it did not live up to expectations.

WHAT I LIKED: Learning about Archimedes screws and how they are used to move sewage and water. The project comes with a booklet that includes instructions and a comic showing how the device works and how it is used in application. I wish there were more explanation of the principles involved. It would have been nice to have a little bit more information about the function of various parts and pieces when putting things together.

I DISLIKED: It's small. Some of the parts are really small and difficult to handle. It requires white glue and ideally, a piece of waxed paper to use as a work surface. Would have been nice if those items were included. It really didn't work so well. On of the pieces of wood in the model I made was insufficiently sloped so the ball bearing wouldn't roll off properly. It worked okay with a little cajoling -- but who wants to cajole?

I did this project with another person. It was fun to work together, but I think this is probably better suited to a solo effort, as the parts are small and you really do need to look at the instruction book closely to figure out what goes where. Also, the project suggests that you purchase a motor -- why not just include the motor in the kit?

Overall, this provided a half hour or so of amusement and I learned something. But it wasn't as much fun as it looked like it might be. Perhaps if I were a twelve-year-old who liked to tinker, I might have a more positive review.
text_fidelity_b: Marbleocity Triple Play Archimedes Screw Marble Machine Kit

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game This game is played a bit different than the regular Monopoly games. There are some similarities though. You get four tokens (and passports), so that seems to limit the number of people who can play. The object of the game is to collect passport stamps - the person to fill their passport first wins. The game starts off with all the major stamps placed on the board - a specific sized one for each property. There are some generic gray stamps that stay in the bank. Landing on a spot you have the option to buy that stamp or it can get auctioned off. When a player lands on a spot that you have the stamp for - the owner is paid a 'Visitor Fee' (basically like rent in the regular game). Another difference are the Here & Now cards and the Chance cards. I think these are what makes the game fun to play. The things the cards can let you do makes the game challenging - just when you think you're going to get ahead, another player can use one of their cards and put a damper on your play. Makes for some lively social interactions (if you get my drift). The dice is a bit different - one die has a icon in the place of the 1 pip (sort of reminds me of the speed die). That icon is the 'Sneaky Swap', it can also still be the 1 in some rolls.

Overall I have to say I've enjoyed trying out this new game (can't say the same for everybody here). I think we're still getting use to the way the game plays compared to regular Monopoly. The games tend to be a bit short - about an hour, but that might be because we still stop a bit and look at the rules to figure out what we're doing. Plus, given the different international locations on the board, we sometimes stop and an go look up where something is. (Helps to keep a globe handy). Fun game - and a bit educational.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. Based solely on the weight of the pieces, you need a few people to put this together. It takes some maneuvering to get the pieces together and in place, but once they are together, they are solid. The swings and ring were a bit high for my 4 year old, so we picked up four 6 inch sections of chain from the local hardware store and some quick links. Problem solved. We left one of the swings higher for the older kids. My son and I swing on it together, and it only moves a bit. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. Seems like commercial quality.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set

Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-hat Café Construction Set with character figures, Building Toys for Kids (328 Pieces) Mega Construx blocks are compatible with LEGO brand blocks, but they have a different focus. In general, they focus on looking nicer, having smaller pieces with smooth edges, and are much more difficult to turn into an off-script creation. Also, they tend to have terrible instruction books, and this kit is no different.

The assembly requires a bit of imagination and guessing, and the kit is not packaged particularly well, as it often requires opening many bags at once to remove the singular small pieces referenced in the manual. Because of this, the kit is harder to assemble than your average LEGO set, but I have to admit that it looks pretty cool when it's done. There are not nearly as many LEGO pegs sticking out as you get on a typical LEGO build, and the figures articulate quite a bit more naturally.

Overall a fun kit for slightly more patient and experienced builders.

text_fidelity_a:
Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange First of all, my 9 year old son LOVED it! The LED lights are amazing and it was easy to watch in the dark at night, or just to enjoy during the day.

The "battery" is very different, you have to hook it up to the black device which has an USB and you need your own adapter to plug and recharge it. Each use lasts maybe 10 minutes max before you need to change batteries and recharge the first one. It is a great way to teach your child to take on different perspectives--if the drone is facing you, your left is actually its' right and your right is it's left. You have to consider that when using the controller just like with RC cars, except it is hard to tell from up in the air. You have to press left or right slightly to figure out which side then rotate it around so you can drive it. It comes with replacement spinners and a small screwdriver.

The return mode is nice, if you are freaking out and afraid it will go into a tree and unable to figure out which way to turn, just press that return button and it will come back to you.

Cons:
1. The drone was able to flip on the first day, but afterwards, for whatever reason, that stopped working. That didn't stop my son from enjoying it.
2. The video/camera app did not work on my phone. I tried different ways to get it to work.
3. Less than a week later, two of the "arms" that connect the ring to the base broke so now it won't lift up correctly. Even with superglue, that didn't help. Unfortunately, it is made of cheap flexible plastic.

So bottom line, I would not recommend buying this item.

This drone is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: 4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange
